title: Insurer Program Agreements Performance Standard — Scorecards, Review, Cure, Suspension and Reinstatement
content:
Each quarter's scorecard under the Insurer Program Agreements compares the network with the targets of the agreement's tier. A scorecard is published once per quarter per agreement and records the publication date, the quarter scored, the average key-to-key days, the customer satisfaction score, the reinspection pass share, the share of repair orders with a supplement, the targets missed and the result, meets or below target.

## 1. Scoring a quarter

The comparison is: average key-to-key days not above the tier's cycle-time target; customer satisfaction score at least the tier's customer satisfaction target; reinspection pass share at least the tier's reinspection pass target; and share of repair orders with a supplement not above the tier's supplement frequency maximum. A target of zero is not scored. A scorecard missing any target is below target.

| Measure | Target met when the quarter's figure is |
|---|---|
| Average key-to-key days | equal to or below the target |
| Customer satisfaction score | equal to or above the target |
| Reinspection pass share | equal to or above the target |
| Supplement frequency | equal to or below the target |

## 2. Opening a review

The consecutive below-target scorecards are counted back from the latest scorecard: the number of below-target scorecards in an unbroken run ending at the latest one. When that number reaches the tier's review trigger, an active agreement goes under review for the tier's cure period in calendar days, counted from the review start date as day zero. The review start date is the first day of the cure period.

Hypothetical runs, oldest first, on a tier whose review trigger is 2:

| Scorecards | Consecutive below-target count | Trigger reached |
|---|---|---|
| meets, below target, below target | 2 | Yes |
| below target, meets, below target | 1 | No |
| below target, below target, meets | 0 | No |

## 3. Closing the review or suspending

The tier's required number of scorecards meeting every target within the cure period return the agreement to active; at the end of the cure period without one, it is suspended, and new assignments stop. Suspension records the suspended date.

Hypothetical count: a review starting on 1 April with a 60-day cure period counts 1 April as day zero and reaches day 60 on 31 May.

## 4. Reinstatement

The waiting period has passed since the suspension. A suspended agreement may be reinstated on an agreed corrective plan once the tier's reinstatement waiting period in calendar days has passed since the suspended date, counted from the suspended date as day zero, with reinstatement on the last waiting day not allowed. Reinstatement returns the agreement to active status.

The waiting period is read from the suspended date on that same agreement's record. With a waiting period of N days, the suspended date is day zero, day N is the last waiting day, and the first day on which reinstatement is allowed is day N plus one.

| Hypothetical suspended date | Waiting period | Last waiting day (not allowed) | First day allowed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 April | 60 days | 31 May | 1 June |
| 1 April | 90 days | 30 June | 1 July |
